items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Earl Hines had a sextet in which I played baritone saxophone.

ctx.x: Okay, well, if anything else occurs. I think Cuban Bennett’s name will come up again. Well, maybe we should deal with that now. Did you play with him in Pittsburgh [Pennsylvania], with Earl Hines?

Oh yes. Yes, I did play with him in Pittsburgh, but not after he came to New York. Yes, that was in 1925. Earl Hines had a sextet in which I played baritone saxophone. Yes, yes, Cuban was in that, but after he came to New York . . .
So that was the only time you worked professionally with him in any capacity?

items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: We didn't hear too much of Earl Hines until later, after he had gone to join Louis Armstrong, that is.

ctx.x: And he was going to sign Earl Hines and he had an orchestra called Baron Lee.
